As a naturally abundant material, BIOX offers a green alternative to synthetic iron oxides, with promising applications in water treatment, pollution control, and resource recovery. However, its efficacy in removing antibiotic contaminants, specifically doxycycline (DOXY), has not been systematically investigated, representing a clear knowledge gap.

title: A green and sustainable incorporation of bi- and ter-thiophenes into 1,4-dihydropyridines: synthetic, mechanistic and photophysical investigations
abstract: Bi- and ter-thiophene moieties have been incorporated into 1,4-dihydropyidines (DHPs) via a novel and green, solvent- free, one pot multi-component Hantzsch reaction. Effect of catalyst, solvents and temperature were studied to optimize the reaction condition. Tetra noctyl ammonium bromide (TOAB) was used as a promoter and trace amount of water inadvertently trapped in ammonium acetate acted as catalyst to facilitate the reaction.

title: An Automated Scholarly Literature Collection Workflow Using Official Services for AI for Science
abstract: AI for Science depends on scientific corpora that can be acquired, checked, and updated reproducibly. This work presents a Python literature collection workflow based on official scholarly services. Crossref and Europe PMC support journal identification and record discovery, NLM PMC Cloud supplies eligible article files and supplementary materials, and separate Elsevier and Wiley adapters use the publishers' official APIs where the operator has the required access.

title: Graphene–ZnO Nanohybrid Synthesis via Wheat Germ Lipase Exfoliation for Environmentally Compatible Antimicrobial Applications
abstract: A graphene-supported ZnO bionanohybrid material (G@WG-ZnO) was prepared through an aqueous synthesis approach using immobilized wheat germ lipase (WG) as a natural biotemplate. The strategy enabled the in-situ formation of ZnO nanoparticles within the graphene-based material. X-ray diffraction, surface and elemental analyses confirmed the formation and incorporation of ZnO, with a Zn content of approximately 6 wt.%.

title: Geometries are forgiving, basins are not: a practical guide to optimizing chemical structures
abstract: A calculated molecular or materials structure is the input to almost every later number in a computational study, yet the step that produces it is usually reported in one line. Two kinds of failure are distinguished here, and the heuristic that follows is offered with its range of validity. Within a basin of the potential energy surface, and for the stiff modes and well-behaved closed-shell systems covered by the benchmarks reviewed, geometries are forgiving in energy: for well-chosen methods, bond lengths converge to a few tenths of a picometer and rotational constants to a few megahertz…

title: Perspective on the Feasibility of Near-Term Quantum Simulation for Industrially Relevant Catalyst Materials
abstract: Quantum simulation has been proposed as a route to treating strongly correlated electronic structure problems relevant to catalysis, but most existing studies focus on faulttolerant algorithms beyond current hardware capabilities. Here we assess the feasibility of near-term quantum simulation for catalytic materials through industrially relevant use cases. We consider zeolite clusters from classical QM/MM simulations relevant to NH3-SCR, and construct electronic active-space and embedding-based models of the catalytic active site.

title: NMRSCOUT: Automated Annotation of Complex Mixtures from Multidimensional NMR Spectra Using Predictive Modelling and Statistical Filtering
abstract: Fast multi-dimensional NMR methods are increasingly used in untargeted metabolomics studies. By mitigating overlap, they offer improved statistical discrimination and/or facilitated biomarker annotation compared to 1D NMR. However, annotating the resulting spectra remains difficult due to limited databases and annotation tools supporting such methods. We introduce NMRSCOUT, an automated workflow for annotating 1D and 2D NMR spectra, including conventional and fast 2D experiments.

title: An Evaluation of Modern Density Functionals for the Bond Dissociation Energies of Diatomic Transition Metal Complexes.
abstract: Two benchmark sets of dissociation energies of diatomic transition-metal complexes have been assembled from previously published data, with selected reference values reassessed or updated where necessary, and used to evaluate a variety of density functionals. The BDE41 set of 41 3d complexes based on both experimental data and phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo reference data is the statistically more robust of the two sets.

title: Engineering Bi2WO6 /NiFe-LDH Heterostructure for Enhanced Water Splitting: Activity, Interfacial Properties and Durability
abstract: Developing efficient and durable electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is essential for advancing sustainable hydrogen production. In this study, we have developed Bi2WO6/NiFe-LDH (BWL) heterostructure as an electrocatalyst toward hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). The catalytic activity was assessed using linear sweep voltammetry (LSV), Tafel analysis, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), electrochemical double-layer capacitance (Cdl), charge-transfer studies and long-term chronopotentiometric measurements.

title: Photochemical Synthesis of Planar-to-Helical BN Acenes
abstract: BN-isosteric acenes offer new opportunities for structural and property modulation, but the synthesis and conformational control of highly fused BN acenes remain challenging. Here we develop a photochemical strategy to convert BN heterocyclic precursors into highly fused BN acenes. By varying substituent positions and ring-fusion orientations, we achieve a conformational evolution from planar to double-helical structures. Despite pronounced backbone distortion, the six-membered BN rings retain substantial local aromaticity.

title: Temperature- and matrix-dependent excited state equilibria in pyrene-linked ruthenium and iridium complexes
abstract: The triplet reservoir effect is an established concept to extend triplet state lifetimes in molecular transition metal complexes. However, the delicate balance between the excited states is impacted by various parameters such as ligand design, the central metal ion, but also the solvent environment. In this study, we present an in-depth investigation of the excited-state nature and relaxation pathways of structurally related Ru(II)- and Ir(III)-based dyads bearing a pyrene moiety in the ligand backbone to serve as triplet reservoir in two different matrices, (frozen) methanol and potassium…

title: Hybrid Kernel/Bath Quantum Dynamics Reveal Conical Intersection Signatures in X-ray Raman Spectroscopy
abstract: Quantum dynamical (QD) descriptions of the coupled electronic and nuclear dynamics can deliver full information on photochemical reactions providing a firm basis for the simulation of their time-resolved spectroscopic signatures. Yet, treating all vibrational degrees of freedom explicitly rapidly becomes computationally intractable. Here, we introduce a hybrid reactive-kernel/bath (RK/B) partitioning of the vibronic Hamiltonian into an anharmonic reactive kernel and a parametrically coupled harmonic bath.

title: When do machine-learning potentials need a configuration-dependent kernel? Learning long-range interactions with Fourier neural operators
abstract: Long-range interactions in machine-learning interatomic potentials are commonly treated by coupling learned sources through either a prescribed electrostatic kernel or a learned but configurationindependent one. Whether such a kernel suffices depends on the underlying screened interaction. We address this question by using Fourier neural operators (FNOs) to learn how latent source fields, built from the descriptors of a local backbone (here MACE), interact across the simulation cell.

title: Yielding Enhanced Gas Sensing in WO3 Thin Films via p-n Heterojunction Formation
abstract: Semiconductor nanostructures have attracted considerable attention for developing high-performance gas sensors for the high-level detection of highly flammable and toxic gases. Herein, the present work integrates n-type WO3 with p-type Ag2O to form a p-n heterojunction by DC reactive magnetron co-sputtering technique. The CH4 sensing performance of the p-n heterojunction with Ag content is correlated with the crystalline structure, surface morphology, elemental composition, optical band gap, and chemical states of the thin film. The p-n heterojunction thin film with 3.63 at.

title: ML/MM
abstract: Electrostatic embedding allows a local machine-learning potential to respond to an extended molecular environment without including every environmental atom in its message-passing graph. We construct a fixed-charge machine-learning/molecular-mechanics (ML/MM) interface for the pretrained MACE-POLAR-1-M model. Analytic Gaussian monopole and dipole operators supply the environmental potential, the internal electrostatic features, and the interaction energy.

title: Time-Resolved Dynamic Assembly and Disassembly of Fueled Peptide Systems
abstract: Many molecules can self-assemble into higher order structures. Depending on the environment, the molecules will either assemble or disassemble towards their equilibrium (lowest) free energy state. Fueled molecular systems allow for a fundamentally di!erent behavior, namely an assembly into a higher free energy state (via the consumption of fuel) and a subsequent disassembly, allowing for new material properties.

title: Stereoselective N-Glycosylation by Iron-Catalyzed Cross-Coupling of Glycosyl Phosphates
abstract: Herein, we report an iron-catalyzed glycosyl cross-coupling strategy for stereoselective β-N-glycosylation through activation of glycosyl phosphate donors under mild conditions. Inspired by the reactivity of enzymes and the biological relevance of phosphate leaving groups, this biomimetic glycosyl phosphate enables efficient coupling of diverse Naglycones with both armed and disarmed sugars. The methodology exhibits broad substrate scope with excellent functional-group tolerance and high β-stereoselectivity.

title: Noncollinear Mixed-Reference Spin-Flip TDDFT: Removing the Dependence on High Exact Exchange
abstract: Collinear mixed-reference spin-flip TDDFT (MRSF-TDDFT) omits the transverse exchange–correlation (xc) response from its spin-flip channel, making large fractions of exact exchange practically necessary. We remove this restriction by incorporating the multicollinear transverse xc kernel into MRSF-TDDFT without empirical rescaling. The U(1) spin-rotation selection rule confines the added response to the matrix blocks within each triplet reference and leaves the inter-reference spin-pairing coupling unchanged.

title: Oxalyl Halide-Mediated Synthesis of Halogenated α,β-Unsaturated γ-Lactams from Amino Acid Derivatives
abstract: An oxalyl halide-mediated conversion of amino acid derivatives to halogenated α,β-unsaturated γ-lactams is reported. The metal-free transformation provides functionalized γ-lactams from readily available amino acid derivatives. Variation of the amine substituent, oxalyl halide, amino acid side chain, and external nucleophile enables independent diversification at N1, C3, C4, and C5, respectively. Mechanistic studies support an activation-cyclization-halogenation sequence involving multiple modes of oxalyl halide reactivity.

title: Peptide Stapling: A Strategy for Enhanced Molecular Recognition of C-Reactive Protein
abstract: In our previous studies, we identified three linear CRP‑binding peptides (P2, P3, and P9), which were subsequently characterized using experimental approaches and in silico analysis. The P3 peptide was successfully used as a sensing element in a microfluidic sensing device for CRP recognition 1. However, linear peptides have some limitations, such as conformational instability. Thus, in our study, we constrained the peptide structure using a stapling approach (P1) to address this problem.

title: Electrochemically assembled oligovalent glycomimetics as potent inhibitors of bacterial sialidases
abstract: Gut microbiota dysbiosis is a hallmark of Crohn’s disease (CD), with increased availability of host-derived nutrients contributing to the expansion of pathogenic bacteria such as adherentinvasive Escherichia coli (AIEC). Microbial sialidases play a key role in mucin degradation by releasing N-acetylneuraminic acid, thereby promoting bacterial nutrient scavenging and colonization. Here, we report a new strategy for targeting intestinal sialidase activity through the development of multivalent glycomimetic inhibitors generated by electrochemically promoted bioconjugation (eY-click).

title: The unifying Role of the “Oxo Wall” concept in Oxygen Evolution Catalysis
abstract: The rational design of catalytic active sites on the surface of solids enables efficient interfacial proton-electron transfer processes in the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and is thus essential for high-performance water splitting on electrolyzer anodes. Popular examples of rational catalyst designs include the Sabatier principle associated with solid-state quantum-chemistry volcano-type reactivity predictions. The use of molecular unifying concepts to predict and rationalize the design of catalytic active OER sites on solid surfaces is rare.

title: trans -1,2-Disubstituted Cyclopropanes with CH 2 -Extended Functional Groups: Synthesis and Physicochemical Properties
abstract: An efficient multigram synthesis of trans -1,2-disubstituted cyclopropane derivatives bearing two functional groups (including fluoroalkyl substituents), with one or both of them attached to the ring through a CH 2 spacer, was developed. The strategy was based on a Michael-initiated ring closure reaction (MIRC), followed by functional group transformations to provide a series of over 70 structurally diverse building blocks, including free carboxylic acids, amines, and other synthetically relevant derivatives, on up to 370 g scale.

title: Multimodal Spectroscopy–Driven Reconstruction of Three-Dimensional Molecular Structures via Conditional Diffusion Model
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) molecular structures underpin molecular function and dynamics. Spectroscopy can encode rich structural information via energy-level transitions, but existing data-driven approaches have largely focused on predicting symbolic representations such as SMILES, or molecular topology rather than reconstructing full 3D structures. Here, we introduce SpecDiffMol, the first generative framework to directly reconstruct full molecular 3D structures from molecular formulae and multimodal spectroscopic data, including infrared, Raman, UV–vis, and NMR spectra.

title: Microstructural evolution, phase transformations and magnetic characteristics of Fe@Fe3O4@NaCl core-shell nanocomposites when varying the EB PVD synthesis temperature
abstract: The manuscript is devoted to a comprehensive study of the physicochemical, structural and magnetic properties of Fe-NaCl nanocomposite systems with an iron content of ~30 wt.%, synthesized by the electron beam physical vapor deposition (EB PVD) method at substrate temperatures (Ts) of 50 °C and 410 °C. Using SEM, STEM/HAADF, EDS, XRD, HRTEM, TGA and Raman spectroscopy, it was proven that the thermodynamic conditions of deposition critically determine the phase composition of nanoinclusions.

title: The efficiency–coverage trade-off of scientific priors in Bayesian search: a registered benchmark on metallic multi-element elasticity data
abstract: Scientific priors speed up Bayesian optimisation in materials discovery, but a prior that steers a small budget toward the materials it favours may miss those it disfavours. We measured this in a benchmark with a registered analysis plan: 7,020 searches (3,000 of them over 3,550 metallic multielement Materials Project structures), for the shear modulus and the specific Young’s modulus, with a historical prior and a composition-only elemental-modulus heuristic, each mixed into expected improvement search with a fixed weight β.

title: Site-Selective Fluorination for Decoupling Oxidative Stability and Ionic Transport of Oxychloride Solid Electrolytes
abstract: Fluorination in solid electrolytes is widely used to enhance oxidative stability owing to fluorine's high electronegativity, yet strong Li–F interactions hinder Li-ion transport. Here we show that this anodic stability–ionic conductivity trade-off can be largely decoupled through lattice-level anion design in the highly Li-ion-conductive LiTaOCl4. By distinguishing oxygen's framework-linking role from chloride's transport-defining role, we targeted fluorination at framework-linking O-sites to minimize perturbation of the Li-ion conduction network.

title: DRAGON: A Versatile Open-Source Software for Diabatization of Multiple Excited States beyond Two Fragments
abstract: The diabatic representation provides a natural framework for describing relevant electronic processes in molecular materials (e.g., optical properties, exciton transport, exciton dissociation, singlet fission, energy transfer between radicals…) using states with a well-defined character (diabatic states) and the electronic couplings between them. This motivates the development of general diabatization methods to generate these diabatic states and couplings.

title: Highly similar urban and rural air quality in West Bengal, India as revealed by statewide sensor network
abstract: The Indo-Gangetic Plain (IGP) suffers from some of the highest air pollution levels in the world. Compared to the upper and central IGP, air pollution in West Bengal, located in the lower IGP, is relatively understudied. This study presents a comprehensive, statewide assessment of air quality across all 23 districts of West Bengal, using India’s first state-commissioned network of 309 sensor stations.

title: The Evolution of Electronic Structure in Conjugated Molecules Revealed by Mixed-Reference Spin-Flip Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory and Density-Based Analyses: I. Polyenes
abstract: Spin-flip time-dependent density functional theory (SF-TDDFT) extends linear-response TDDFT to diradicals, bond breaking, conical intersections, and excited states with doubly excited character. The mixed-reference SF-TDDFT (MRSF-TDDFT) formulation provides spin-purified states while keeping the simplicity of the original formalism. Previous benchmarks of MRSF-TDDFT have focused on energies, structures, and permanent and transition dipole moments. Here we look at the state and transition densities.

title: Binary MOF micropatterns enabling spatially defined dual dye encapsulation
abstract: We report a patterning strategy that combines X-ray lithography with ceramic-to-MOF conversion for the fabrication of binary metal-organic framework (MOF) micropatterns composed of the pillar-layered MOF Cu 2 (BDC 0.5 (Br 2 BDC) 0.5 ) 2 DABCO and HKUST-1. The fabrication protocol enables spatially controlled integration of two MOF phases within defined microscale architectures. Further, the selective encapsulation of distinct fluorescent dyes within each MOF results in micropatterns exhibiting localized dual-wavelength emission.

title: DFT Studies of the Structural and Electronic Properties of Fluorinated and Methoxylated 3-Amino-2-CyclopropylQuinazolin-4(3H)-one Molecules
abstract: DFT B3LYP/6-31+G(d,p) calculations were performed on the twelve fluorinated and methoxylated 3-amino-2-cyclopropylquinazolin-4(3H)-one molecules, which are abbreviated as FMACQs, in toluene, the gas phase, and aqueous solution. title: CFD Evaluation of a Tesla-Type Micromixer for Chemical Processing
abstract: Passive Tesla-type micromixers achieve very good mixing in published studies, yet they are rarely found in industrial flow reactors. This study evaluates whether a modified Tesla micromixer could be suitable for continuous chemical processing by considering mixing quality together with pressure drop and throughput. A three-dimensional model with four pairs of Tesla units (channel width 200 µm, depth 110 µm) was built from published dimensions and simulated as a transient, incompressible, laminar water flow in SimScale at Reynolds numbers of 10, 50 and 70.

title: Molecular Mechanics-Based Symmetric Two-State Energy-Gap Estimation of Binding Free Energies
abstract: We examine a symmetric two-state energy-gap (STEG) approximation for binding free energies using a molecular mechanics/Poisson–Boltzmann surface area (MM/PBSA) energetic baseline. An endpoint linear-response approximation, together with a negligible OFF-state mean gap, yields an estimate equal to one-half of the MM/PBSA energetic baseline. The numerical protocol requires one 50 ns bound trajectory per complex and no simulations at intermediate coupling states.

title: A Density-Matrix Formulation of Vibrational Circular Dichroism Spectra for Møller-Plesset and Configuration Interaction Methods
abstract: We reformulate the overlap of wave-function derivatives that defines the atomic axial tensors (AATs) and velocity-gauge atomic polar tensors (VG-APTs) used to compute vibrational circular dichroism (VCD) rotatory strengths. In place of our earlier determinant-level derivatives, the new approach expresses these tensors as contractions involving molecular-orbital derivative integrals, perturbed and unperturbed one- and two-electron density matrices, and dot products of the perturbed correlated wave-function amplitudes. Following the elegant treatment of the diagonal Born-Oppenheimer correction by Gauss and co-workers, the formulation holds for any real, normalized CI-like wave function. The two-electron density contribution vanishes exactly, because one perturbation is real (nuclear) and the other imaginary (magnetic field or momentum); this removes multiple terms from our earlier AAT and VG-APT expressions for second-order Møller-Plesset perturbation theory (MP2) and configuration interaction singles and doubles (CISD). We also present a simplified form of the origin-independent length-gauge [LG(OI)] rotatory strength that avoids the singular-value decomposition of the outer product of the length-gauge APT and VG-APT vectors for each mode, and that clarifies how the LG(OI) and velocity-gauge rotatory strengths are related. Applying the density-based AATs and VG-APTs to ($P$)-hydrogen peroxide, (\textit{S})-methyloxirane, and (\textit{S})-3-chloro-1-butyne, we find that discrepancies among the gauges arise chiefly from basis-set incompleteness in the VG-APT. The charge-sum rule serves as a useful measure of that incompleteness, independent of the correlation method.

title: Interfacial intelligence: A new way to design polymer brushes
abstract: Polymer brushes are dense layers of polymer chains that can be engineered to change how a surface interacts with its surroundings. By controlling interactions with water, ions, proteins and other materials, they can reduce friction, prevent unwanted materials from sticking, improve separation and support the functionality of sensors and other devices.

title: Amorphous Halide Cathodes Enable 75C All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
abstract: Power delivery in all-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs) is often pursued by maximizing the bulk ionic conductivity of cathode active materials (CAMs), while grain-boundary (GB) ion-transport barriers caused by lattice mismatch remain a major kinetic bottleneck. Here, we reveal that minimizing GB transport barriers, rather than simply enhancing intrinsic conductivity, unlocks ultrafast ion-transport in halide CAMs. Amorphization converts crystalline LiVCl4 into a conformal amorphous phase that preserves short-range V–Cl coordination while minimizing long-range ion-transport tortuosity.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Mechanistic Insights of Electroreductive Cobalt-Catalyzed Asymmetric Radical Addition
abstract: Transition-metal-catalyzed asymmetric electroreduction has emerged as a compelling platform for enantioselective C–C bond formation, with notable advances in electroreductive cross-coupling. Translating this success to stereocontrolled radical additions across unsaturated bonds remains a formidable challenge, particularly for the construction of fully substituted stereogenic carbon centers. Herein, we report an electroreductive, cobalt-catalyzed asymmetric radical addition of diverse organohalides to α-imino esters.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Understanding the role of IQ motif-containing GTPase-activating protein 1 as a potential disruptor of the essential adhesion module at cell-cell junctions
abstract: A key mechanism of stabilization of Cadherin-based cell-cell adhesions is through a mechanically modulated interaction to cortical actin filaments. This interaction is facilitated by a cytoplasmic adhesion module comprising of a complex of {beta}-catenin/-catenin. Recent evidence shows that under specific conditions the {beta}-catenin/-catenin complex gets disrupted because of mechanical disregulation of the junction maintenance machinery. The IQ motif-containing GTPase-activating protein 1 (IQGAP1) plays apparently a vital role as an internal regulator of the adhesion module, which competes for binding on {beta}-catenin with -catenin and is able to dissociate the latter from the adhesion complex. The underlying molecular mechanism is poorly understood with no clear evidence on what types of interactions are critical for a potential disruption. In this work, we combine steered-molecular-dynamics simulations and a multi-step protein-protein docking framework to dissect how mechanical detachment of -catenin from the adhesion complex modulates the interactions between IQGAP1 and {beta}-catenin. Our simulations show that as -catenin detaches from {beta}-catenin, IQGAP1 docks with progressively favorable scores. Interfacial analysis and subsequent mutagenesis studies, allow us to predict a molecular mechanism for an IQGAP1-driven disruption of the junctional adhesion module that centers on early onset of key favorable electrostatic interactions.

title: PatentAgentBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents with Professional Patent Task Suites
abstract: Patent practice lies at the intersection of technical, legal, and linguistic work, making it challenging yet crucial to technological innovation. Recently, rapid advances in large language models (LLMs) and agentic systems have demonstrated the potential to complete realistic business workflows and even patent works. This raises a question: can current AI systems perform patent work reliably? Existing benchmarks cover a limited range of patent tasks and simplify evidence acquisition by providing reference materials or candidate documents. In this paper, we introduce PatentAgentBench, a benchmark comprising 510 instances across eight task suites: novelty search, freedom-to-operate (FTO) search, design FTO, invalidity search, claim charting, patent drafting, office-action response, and patent translation. Curated from real patent records and professional materials, the benchmark combines task-specific metrics with expert-reviewed annotations and rubrics. Retrieval tasks such novelty search, FTO, etc., require agents to search and compare patent collections without a supplied candidate pool. The drafting and OAR tasks assess the quality of agents' work given technical disclosure and office action notice. We evaluate seven LLMs across four agent harnesses on PatentAgentBench, finding that current systems still struggle to identify novelty, assess risk, and understand practitioner intent throughout patent workflows.

title: Toward Fast Human Reaction Modeling from High-Frequency Digital Interaction Data
abstract: We investigate whether limbic-like signatures of rapid, salience-driven behavior can be identified in high-resolution Counter-Strike 2 telemetry. This exploratory study introduces Ego-Knowledge, a leak-reduced reconstruction of each player's plausible perceptual state, supported by a millisecond-precision visibility engine and a reaction-centered extraction pipeline. Using a neuroscience-motivated 60--120 ms window, we derive coarse fight-or-flight labels from visibility- and damage-triggered events, with back-damage cases enabling constrained reaction-time analysis and manual label checks. We train two telemetry-native models using only information available by the trigger: EMBER (gradient boosting) and ORBIT (a custom transformer). On the full validation set, EMBER achieves 73.5% accuracy and ORBIT 71.2%, versus a 51.5% majority-class baseline, and both generalize to held-out players. The strongest LLM baseline achieves 62.7% on 1,000 validation cases; on these same cases, EMBER (73.6%) and ORBIT (70.9%) perform better (McNemar p=1.3e-9 and 1.5e-6, respectively), with orders-of-magnitude lower inference time and cost, though the comparison is not compute-matched. Including a short post-trigger window changes forecasting into early response recognition, raising accuracy monotonically to 85.15%. We propose this curve as a candidate probe of the transition from rapid to deliberative control, but roughly uniform per-tick gains do not establish that interpretation. The neuroscience framing is hypothesis-generating, not mechanistic: physiological ground truth, suitable control distributions, and reverse-inference limitations remain open. We outline extensions to auditory reconstruction, larger datasets, and telemetry-native foundation models.

title: Temperature-dependent magnetic properties of the antiferromagnet Mn$_2$Au
abstract: Mn$_2$Au is one of the most promising materials for antiferromagnetic spintronics due to its high Néel temperature, moderate anisotropy, layered spin structure allowing current induced spin-orbit-torques, and ultrafast spin dynamics. Further understanding and control of the magnetic order in Mn$_2$Au for ultrafast spintronics applications via ultrashort electric/optical means requires accurate understanding of how its magnetic properties depend on temperature. Here we present atomistic spin dynamics simulations of the temperature-dependent macroscopic magnetic properties of Mn$_2$Au single crystals. We introduce a spin Hamiltonian based on previous ab initio calculations which produces temperature-dependent scaling of the anisotropy constants with magnetisation consistent with Zener-Akulov-Callen-Callen power laws. The calculated temperature dependence of exchange stiffness follows a scaling law with magnetisation of $m^{1.83}_e$ , and predicts a temperature-dependent domain wall width that agrees very well with direct simulation. Our model provides an understanding of temperature-dependent magnetic properties of Mn$_2$Au that enables large-scale simulation of the working conditions of spintronic devices.

title: AutoEnergyDesign: An LLM-Driven Agent for Automatic Energy System Design Optimization
abstract: Designing building energy systems is a high-dimensional, mixed-integer search problem: when each design is evaluated by a year-long simulation, black-box optimizers typically need hundreds of evaluations. This paper presents AutoEnergyDesign, a framework in which a Large Language Model (LLM) agent reasons over previous simulation results, proposes configuration changes and learns in context from each outcome, while a git-based mechanism automatically reverts unsuccessful changes. The agent couples a reasoning model with an explicit memory organisation (procedural, semantic, episodic and reflective), a constrained action interface and an environment-grounded keep/revert signal. The simulator covers eight technologies (photovoltaics, micro-wind, combined heat and power, solar thermal, gas boilers, batteries, heat pumps and inverters) and computes the 25-year Net Present Cost (NPC), including capital and operating costs and salvage value. On a case study with measured building load profiles, the agent, run with Claude Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 (ten runs of 50 simulations each), is compared with random search, Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) Bayesian optimization and a $(1+1)$ evolution strategy sharing the agent's acceptance rule (300 evaluations, ten seeds). With all three models the agent reaches an NPC of about 3.53 MEUR, 1.20% below the best TPE result and 0.23% below the best evolution-strategy result. It comes within 1% of this design after a median of 18 (Opus) to 27.5 (Haiku) simulations, whereas among the baselines only the evolution strategy does so, in half of its seeds and after a median of 192 evaluations. Opus reaches the best design in all ten runs, Sonnet in six (two runs never come within 1%), and Haiku comes within 1% in every run but reaches it exactly only once. Every decision is recorded in an auditable trace.

title: Accelerating SO(2)-Equivariant Materials Models through Low-Precision Emulation
abstract: Rotationally equivariant architectures improve the physical fidelity of machine-learned (ML) universal materials models based on graph neural networks (GNNs). However, their scalability is limited by the use of non-trivial, high-precision tensor operations during both training and inference. Adopting the reduced-precision formats of matrix multiplication units (MMUs), e.g., FP8 instead of FP32, provides massive increases in throughput, up to 30x (60x) on NVIDIA Hopper (Blackwell) GPUs, but may lead to drastic loss of accuracy. Here, we introduce tailored 'emulated' low-precision operations under the integer Ozaki scheme to accelerate the 'SO(2)-equivariant' processing layers of GNNs, which dominate the runtime of (1) many state-of-the-art ML interatomic potentials (MLIPs) and (2) most universal ML Hamiltonian (MLH) models. Our framework, FlashSO(2), outperforms TF32, the most accurate native low-precision MMU format, in throughput, accuracy, and memory footprint at once. At the SO(2) layer level, it reaches 40x (7x) the throughput of MALOQ's (UMA's) reference implementation, an MLH (MLIP) model, sustaining up to 236 (232) effective Tflop/s on an NVIDIA GH200, 3.5x the FP32 peak. At the model level, FlashSO(2) helps train MALOQ 3.9x faster than its pure-FP32 version while reducing peak memory by 58% at no loss in accuracy. In molecular dynamics simulations with UMA, the speedup factor is 3.3x, and the peak memory is reduced by 51%. FlashSO(2) thus pushes the speed-accuracy Pareto frontier of equivariant materials models beyond the native low-precision formats and substantially lowers the resources required to exploit their scaling laws.

title: Biology-Guided Context-Aware Residual Propagation for Spatial Gene Expression Prediction from Histology
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics provides spatially resolved molecular profiling, but its cost, limited throughput and experimental complexity hinder routine large-scale use. Predicting spatial gene expression from hematoxylin-and-eosin-stained histology images offers a scalable alternative, yet remains challenging because histology provides only an indirect morphological view of molecular activity. Existing methods typically decode expression from visual features in a single stage, even when enhanced with spatial aggregation, retrieval or multi-resolution fusion. This formulation is restrictive because spot-level expression reflects not only local morphology but also cellular identity, neighborhood composition and tissue-level organization. We propose BCARP, a Biology-guided Context-Aware Residual Propagation framework for histology-guided spatial transcriptomics prediction. Instead of directly predicting gene expression from histology embeddings, BCARP treats them as morphology visual priors and progressively refines spot representations in a transcriptomics-oriented latent space. Each refinement step integrates nuclei-guided local cellular context with prototype-guided global context propagation, enabling information exchange across both neighboring and spatially distant spots. A pattern-scale decoder further separates spatial expression into pattern prediction from raw expression with scale calibration. Evaluated on three ST datasets and ten HEST-1k cohorts, BCARP achieves the highest mean correlation-based performance against other baselines. Numerical results support biology-guided local-global residual propagation as an effective alternative to visual decoding for histology-to-transcriptomics prediction.

title: Subspace Crystallization in Grokking: Rank Compression Tracks the Phase Transition
abstract: Grokking describes understanding something deeply and intuitively. In neural networks, it is the phenomenon where a network generalizes long after memorizing its training data. This delay has been linked to a fall in the effective rank of the network's weight matrices, but whether this rank compression drives grokking or follows it is still unresolved. We study a mean-field MLP and a one-layer transformer trained on modular arithmetic and observe that: (i) Compression follows the onset, not memorization. Every transformer memorizes its training data within 250 steps, while the grokking onset (the first step at which test accuracy reaches 95%) varies from 6,500 to 21,000 steps. The steepest fall in effective rank comes about 900 steps after the onset, however late the onset occurs, and networks that memorize without grokking compress far less. (ii) Subspace crystallization. We call the span of the fewest top singular directions of a weight matrix that preserve 99% of test accuracy its sufficient subspace. Its size can shrink as the margin between the correct and the best wrong output grows, so we also count the directions needed to keep the outputs within 10%. In the transformer, this count falls during the transition from a quarter or more of the available directions to about a tenth, which we call subspace crystallization. (iii) Imposing low rank does not speed up grokking. Against a factorized full-rank control, capping the rank of the transformer's MLP input weights delays the onset, and capping the rank of its embedding stops 15 of 20 runs from grokking. Compression is therefore a signature of grokking rather than its cause.

title: Nonlocal Einstein Relation in Confined Phonon Hydrodynamics
abstract: Einstein relations connect carrier mobility to macroscopic transport coefficients and constitute a fundamental link between microscopic dynamics and transport. In phonon hydrodynamics, this connection is conventionally local: the drift-induced thermal conductivity is proportional to the local drift mobility. Here we show that this relation becomes intrinsically nonlocal under spatial confinement. We derive a nonlocal Einstein relation, $κ_H(y) = \int P(y-y')μ(y'),dy'$, in which hydrodynamic thermal conductivity $κ_H(y)$ at one position depends on collective drift mobility $μ(y')$ across the entire cross-section of the channel. In the small-Knudsen-number limit, our nonlocal theory recovers the viscous heat equation and the local Einstein relation. At finite Knudsen number, nonlocality produces intrinsic boundary slip and distinct size-scaling behavior of the drift mobility $μ$ and hydrodynamic thermal conductivity $κ_H(y)$. First-principles calculations for graphite show that nonlocality broadens the channel-size window over which thermal conductivity exhibits superlinear size dependence. Temperature-dependent simulations further show that the nonlocal theory captures the emergence of a hydrodynamic peak in thermal conductivity normalized by ballistic conductance, whereas the local theory fails to accurately predict its magnitude. Our results establish a microscopic connection between collective phonon mobility and heat conduction beyond local hydrodynamics.

title: Hybrid quantum-classical machine learning potential with variational quantum circuits
abstract: Machine learning potentials (MLPs) based on equivariant message-passing neural networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracy for atomistic simulation, yet integration of variational quantum circuit (VQC) readouts into such frameworks remains unexplored for condensed-matter systems. Here we employ and characterize a hybrid quantum-classical MLP (HQC-MLP) by coupling an E(3)-equivariant message-passing network with VQC readout layers for predicting DFT energies and forces of liquid silicon (64 atoms, periodic cell, 2000-3000 K).

title: How the US midterm elections could impact chemistry and other sciences
abstract: Democrats will likely ramp up oversight hearings and attempt to pass legislation on bipartisan issues like data centers and pesticides, analysts say

title: Hydrogen production from seawater: Low-cost catalyst could cut energy use and resist corrosion
abstract: Using a range of advanced characterization techniques, researchers say they have developed a novel method with the potential to produce hydrogen from seawater using a process that requires less energy, resists corrosion and could support more economical hydrogen production.

title: Beyond Prediction: Mechanism-Guided Artificial Intelligence for Drug Repurposing and Translational Pharmacology
abstract: Drug repurposing offers an efficient strategy for identifying new therapeutic applications for existing medicines. Advances in artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, and systems pharmacology have enabled the analysis of complex biological and clinical datasets to identify potential drug–disease associations. However, conventional predictive models often lack mechanistic interpretability, limiting their translational reliability.

title: An 'electron waiting room' helps blue titanium dioxide hold light energy longer
abstract: To produce hydrogen using sunlight, the energy obtained from light must be retained until it can be used in a chemical reaction. However, if an electron that has gained energy from light quickly returns to its original position, it becomes difficult to make use of that energy.

title: DockBind: A Quality-Controlled Data Set of Modeled Protein–Ligand Complexes Associated with Affinity Data
abstract: Ligand–protein interaction prediction is essential for structure-based drug discovery, but further development of machine-learning scoring functions is limited by a lack of high-quality training data sets. Here, we present DockBind, a curated data set of modeled protein–ligand complexes paired with experimental binding affinity data, generated through a quality-controlled docking workflow. This workflow was developed based on an expanded docking benchmark, where we systematically evaluated free and template-based docking methods as well as ligand similarity and maximum common substructure (MCS)-based pose filtering to generate and identify the most realistic poses. The resulting workflow was then incorporated into a pipeline integrating structural and binding affinity data from Binding MOAD, the Protein Data Bank, ChEMBL, and BindingDB, which resulted in 18,332 complexes across 612 protein targets, with high structural reliability and chemical diversity─the DockBind data set─providing a valuable resource for training and benchmarking machine-learning scoring functions.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: The Emerging Potential of Janus-Type Di-N-heterocyclic Carbene Transition Metal Complexes in Homogeneous Catalysis
abstract: The article explores the catalytic potential of the emerging class of Janus-type di-N-heterocyclic carbenes that have attracted attention in recent times. The article details different aspects of these Janus-type di-N-heterocyclic carbenes particularly from their classifications, expansion in synthesis approaches, to finally their utility in different homogeneous transformations.

title: Next-Generation Brain Health Monitoring Enabled by Integrated Wearable AI Infrastructure
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases are difficult to detect during their pre-symptomatic stages, when intervention is most effective. Advances in wearable biosensors, artificial intelligence (AI), and neuroscience now enable continuous monitoring of brain-related physiological signals in real-world settings. However, progress in sensing technologies, signal analytics, and machine learning remains fragmented, limiting the biological specificity, robustness, and clinical translation of many digital biomarkers. This review presents an integrated framework that links molecular pathology and neural circuit dysfunction to sensor-detectable digital phenotypes across sleep, autonomic regulation, gait, speech, and ocular dynamics. We evaluate emerging wearable platforms, including bioelectric, optical, and neuromotor sensors, and discuss critical design considerations such as signal quality, user-centered form factors, and ultra-low-power edge AI systems. We further examine how self-supervised learning, federated AI, mechanistic modeling, and fairness-aware validation can improve biomarker reliability, interpretability, and generalizability. To facilitate clinical deployment, we introduce the Personalized Brain-Health Operating System (pBH-OS), a privacy-preserving reference architecture for scalable digital phenotyping. The framework maps conceptual layers to existing technologies while identifying key validation gaps. We also address practical challenges, including adherence, device dropout, informative missingness, regulatory compliance, and accountability. Together, these advances provide a pathway toward biologically grounded and regulation-ready systems capable of identifying neurodegenerative risk years before clinical symptom onset.
keywords: Bio‐Signal Monitoring, And Remote Patient Monitoring

title: Insights into Composition-Induced Structural Shifts in Lipid Nanoparticles
abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are a leading platform for nucleic acid delivery, yet current formulations typically suffer from rapid in vivo clearance and limited extrahepatic delivery. Recent experiments demonstrate that increasing the helper lipid content (e.g., to 40% 1,2-distearoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine [DSPC]) can significantly improve mRNA stability, prolong circulation, and enhance transfection efficiency. In this study, we used coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to provide mechanistic insight into the structural changes driving these improvements. Our simulations confirm that an elevated helper lipid content fundamentally alters the internal morphology of the LNP. Consistent with experimental observations, at high DSPC levels, the core transitions from a compact, disordered, predominantly lipid state to an extended structure with distinct lamellar-like elements encompassing lipid-rich and water-rich regions. This structural reorganization can be used to rationalize the enhanced stability and delivery properties reported in the experiments. These findings provide a molecular-level understanding of the composition-morphology relationship and suggest that coarse-grained modeling can inform the design of novel LNP formulations.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Machine learning-based stability optimization design and virtual screening of the anti-pulmonary fibrosis peptide DR3penA
abstract: The novel anti-fibrotic peptide DR3penA, previously developed by our research group, demonstrates substantial therapeutic potential; however, its inherent limited metabolic stability in vivo, attributable to its linear structure, hinders clinical translation. Although cyclization represents a key strategy for enhancing peptide structural rigidity, exhaustive trial-and-error exploration across the vast chemical modification space entails prohibitive computational and experimental costs.

title: Sulfonium-decorated antifungals break the mold
abstract: The chemical tweak helped the compound evade resistance in fungi that had infected larvae

title: NeCS-Flow: Necrosis-Guided Contrast-Enhanced MRI Synthesis with Rectified-Flow Refinement
abstract: Background: Gadolinium-based contrast agents raise concerns about tissue deposition, adverse reactions, and increased costs. Purpose: To develop and validate a deep learning pipeline for gadolinium-free post-contrast T1w brain MRI synthesis incorporating necrotic scaling and Posterior-Mean Rectified Flow (PMRF) refinement, and to evaluate diagnostic utility through a blinded multi-reader study. Study Type: Retrospective. Population: 454 patients with adult-type gliomas (grade 2-4) from four publicly available datasets.

title: Predicting Protein-Protein Interactions Using Vectorized Sequence Descriptors and Machine Learning Classifiers
abstract: Accurate prediction of protein-protein interactions (PPIs) is fundamental for elucidating cellular mechanisms and accelerating drug discovery. Although experimental techniques provide extensive interaction maps, their high cost and time requirements necessitate robust computational alternatives. In this study, we present an interpretable machine-learning framework that integrates sequence-derived descriptors, specifically 120 Auto-Covariance (AC) features, 686 Conjoint Triad (CT) features, and 1,820 Local Descriptors (LD) features, with classical classification algorithms, including Support…

title: Auditable Corridor Shortlisting under Partial Observability: A Systems Approach to Ranking Human Trafficking Origin–Destination Links
abstract: International human trafficking is only partially observed at the corridor level: a small number of origin–destination (OD) pairs appear in public victim-case compilations, while the space of possible corridors is vast. We treat corridor pri-oritization as a systems problem and present an auditable ranking loop that maps sparse observed ODs, country-level covariates, and an explicit graph representation into a shortlist of corridors for subsequent review.

title: Predictive Inorganic Synthesis Based on Machine Learning Using Small Data Sets: A Case Study of Hydrodynamic Diameter-Controlled Copper Nanoparticles
abstract: Copper nanoparticles (Cu NPs) have a broad applicability, yet their synthesis is sensitive to subtle changes in reaction parameters. This sensitivity, combined with the time- and resource-intensive nature of experimental optimization, poses a major challenge in achieving reproducible and size-controlled synthesis. While machine learning (ML) shows promise in materials research, its application is often limited by scarcity of large high-quality experimental data sets.

title: Silent bacterial genes yield potential leads for future cancer drugs
abstract: Natural products produced by microorganisms are a promising source of new drugs. Researchers at the Helmholtz Center for Infection Research (HZI) and its Saarbrücken-based site, the Helmholtz Institute for Pharmaceutical Research Saarland (HIPS), have now discovered a new family of such compounds, elucidated their unusual biosynthesis and developed a way to produce them synthetically.

title: Alloy-Assisted Formation of Vanadium-Rich Thiophosphates with Enhanced Charge Transport and Glassy Magnetism
abstract: Vanadium-based thiophosphates in the MPQ3/M2P2Q6 family provide an unusual platform for coupling mixed-metal valence, metal vacancies, and 2D magnetism, but access to phase-pure multimetal solid solutions with verified chemical homogeneity remains limited. Here, we show that multication alloying provides a route to incorporating V into layered thiophosphates while retaining the mixed-valent, vacancy-containing character of V2−xP2S6. This approach yields Fe1.25V0.6P2S6, Ni1.25V0.6P2S6, Co1.25V0.6P2S6, and high-entropy V-containing compositions.

title: Direct observation of a spin-polarized surface Dirac gap in the antiferromagnetic topological insulator NdBi
abstract: A gapped Dirac cone in antiferromagnetic topological insulators (AFM-TIs) is essential for realizing the quantized anomalous Hall effect, yet its intrinsic magnitude remains controversial. In the prototypical AFM-TI MnBi2Te4, however, the observed Dirac gap is significantly smaller than theoretical predictions or nearly absent, highlighting a long-standing discrepancy. Here we demonstrate that NdBi hosts a spin-polarized topological surface Dirac cone with a sizable gap of 17 meV at the Dirac point, in excellent agreement with density functional theory predictions (12 meV). This direct observation is enabled by high-resolution 7 eV laser-based spin- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, which unambiguously disentangles the spin-polarized surface Dirac cone from bulk-derived states. Furthermore, through temperature dependence and controlled surface contamination, we establish a direct linkage between surface magnetism and the Dirac gap, demonstrating that the gap opens only in the presence of surface magnetic order. These results provide definitive spectroscopic evidence for an intrinsic Dirac gap in AFM-TIs and establish NdBi as a model platform to resolve the long-standing discrepancy between experiment and theory in AFM-TIs.

title: MMB-DTI: A Multimodal State Space Framework with Bidirectional Cross-Attention for Drug-Target Interaction Prediction
abstract: Accurate drug-target interaction (DTI) prediction is fundamental to computational drug discovery. However, existing deep learning methods typically oversimplify biochemical entities as 1D sequences, neglecting crucial spatial topologies, and incur prohibitive quadratic computational costs when modeling long-range protein dependencies. To overcome these bottlenecks, we propose MMB-DTI, a novel multimodal framework that synergistically fuses evolutionary and chemical semantics, extracted via pre-trained language models (ESM-2 and ChemBERTa), with structural topologies derived from graph neural…
venue: IEEE transactions on computational biology and bioinformatics

title: Decoding Capacity Regeneration in Zinc-Silver Batteries: Gas-Guided Multi-Physics Modeling and Hybrid AI Prediction
abstract: Accurately predicting battery life is vital for next-generation energy storage. Zinc-silver batteries (ZSBs) offer high power and energy density but suffer from short cycle life due to parasitic oxygen and hydrogen evolution reactions (OER/HER) that cause irreversible swelling. Here, we uncover a counterintuitive capacity regeneration phenomenon in ZSBs under a 20°C scenario: a regime where conventional degradation models fail. By establishing a monitoring system, we capture synchronized electrical, strain, gas concentration, pressure, and temperature signals.

title: Valorization of Brassica juncea waste into iron oxide nanoparticles for efficient hexavalent chromium [Cr(VI)] remediation: characterization, experimental kinetics, isotherms, and machine learning optimization
abstract: Hexavalent chromium [Cr(VI)] has emerged as a significant environmental pollutant because of its toxicity and long-term persistence. As a result, remediation of Cr(VI) is urgently needed to save the ecosystem and human health. There are several traditional remediation methods that are not sustainable. Therefore, the current work explores the green synthesis of iron oxide nanoparticles (BJ-IONPs) derived from Mustard (Brassica juncea) waste.

title: When Can a Learned Design Surrogate Be Trusted in a Self-Driving Microfluidics Laboratory? An Offline Closed-Loop Framework Built and Tested on Six Public Tables
abstract: Self-driving laboratories couple a learned design surrogate to an instrument, and on every new target domain it must answer four questions: when it can be trusted, how many target measurements it needs, which to make first, and when to stop adapting, switch models or escalate. We state a framework making each measurable (a competence ratio, a budget $k^*(\varepsilon)$, a time-to-target and a priced decision) and instantiate it without wet experiments on six public droplet-microfluidic and liposome tables as offline laboratories: 107 leave-one-group tiers whose rows are hidden labels. A sealed, pre-registered programme (two sealed negative validations and a pre-registered test on three more tables) and seven frozen closed-loop protocols, each run twice, yield 23 findings. Shift cost is stratified by shift type; no label-free statistic certifies individual candidates; random-split model-family rankings predicted neither the sealed nor the loop rankings. Warm-start residual boosting returns a surrogate to $1.25\times$ its development reference within 20 target rows in 94% of chemistry tiers (27% under a strict noise-floor reading), 90% of laboratory and 40% of device tiers, and a budget planned from the shift type on other tables is not measurably worse on a new one. In the loop, one gain survives drift and shuffled-label controls on all tiers, carried by the sparsely sampled ones: proposing at once and warm-starting on every measurement reaches a 10% target in 2.80 measurements against 3.31 for the reference, and in 5.72 against 11.35 for random proposals on 301 hard units at a 3% tolerance. No label-free acquisition rule survives the shuffled-label control, no interval-aware proposal or other model family does better, and no threshold rule on the tested diagnostics beats always continuing once escalation is priced. No wet-lab validation is claimed.

title: Spin Relaxation and Electrical Control of Spin Transport in Few-Layer $T_{\rm d}$-MoTe$_2$
abstract: We report electrical tuning of spin relaxation in atomically thin $T_{\rm d}$-MoTe$_2$, a representative low-symmetry transition metal dichalcogenide. Weak antilocalization measurements reveal strong spin--orbit interaction with spin--orbit lengths of tens of nanometers, consistent with recent theoretical predictions. Despite the semimetallic nature of $T_{\rm d}$-MoTe$_2$, in the ultrathin limit the spin--orbit scattering time can be tuned electrostatically by up to threefold. We further investigate vertical electric field effects on the spin--orbit length and time, and demonstrate the modulation of the Rashba parameters. Relation between spin--orbit scattering time and the diffusion coefficient indicates that spin relaxation is governed by the D'yakonov--Perel' mechanism in both monolayer and bilayer $T_{\rm d}$-MoTe$_2$. These results establish few-layer $T_{\rm d}$-MoTe$_2$ as a platform for electrically tunable spin transport, thereby providing insight into spin relaxation in low-symmetry transition metal dichalcogenides.

title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors
abstract: Buried interfaces play a critical role in the operational stability of perovskite optoelectronic devices, yet remain challenging to probe non-destructively. Here, we demonstrate a multiwavelength photoluminescence-based approach exploiting the wavelength-dependent absorption of perovskites, enabling fast, and non-destructive probing of depth-sensitive degradation behavior of perovskite devices under operational conditions. Using ultraviolet (UV) light-soaking with different indium tin oxide (ITO) modifiers as a test case, we employ wide-field photoluminescence (PL) imaging, time-resolved photoluminescence (trPL) and ideality factor measurements with different wavelength excitation to characterize degradation behavior of both perovskite thin films and photovoltaic devices under UV soaking. Using only nondestructive characterization, we show that UV-induced degradation in p-i-n perovskite solar cells occurs preferentially at the HTL interface, adversely affecting device stability, consistent with ex-situ destructive tests. Our results also show that modifying the buried interface with 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane reduces UV-induced damage at the buried interface, thus improving the UV stability of both perovskite films and devices. This work establishes a fast, non-destructive strategy to screen depth-dependent degradation in perovskite devices, offering insights for interface design and stability optimization.

title: Oxygen partial pressure induced dielectric phase evolution in PLD deposited Barium Strontium Titanate thin films
abstract: Barium Strontium Titanate ((BaxSr1-x)TiO3, BST) thin films are amongst the most extensively studied dielectric alloys over the last decade. This is due to the tunability of the dielectric constant and dissipation factor in the underlying ferroelectric and paraelectric states. One important feature of BST is that the competition between the ferroelectric BaTiO3 and the paraelectric SrTiO3 parent phases can be tuned by the A-site alloy concentration, opening a platform for exploring dielectric phase competition. However, the understanding of the interplay between and establishing the control of the dielectric phase from thin film deposition parameters has not been sufficiently reported in the literature. Here, we synthesized a series of SrRuO3/BST/SrRuO3 epitaxial thin film heterostructures by Pulsed Laser Deposition (PLD) from a (Ba0.9Sr0.1)TiO3 target under systematic variation of the oxygen partial pressure during the BST deposition. We mapped the dielectric phase of the film to the oxygen growth pressure, film composition, and film crystal structure. A ferroelectric, relaxor-like, or paraelectric phase can be obtained with relatively moderate change in oxygen growth pressure. Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) analysis further indicates that this pressure-dependent phase evolution is accompanied by a structural transition of the BST lattice from tetragonal toward a nearly cubic phase, with the latter corresponding to the relaxor-like state. The control of the dielectric phase opens a pathway to study phase evolution and enable future computing technologies.

title: A Local Stabilized Isogeometric Formulation with Discontinuous Pressure for Mesh-Conforming and Immersed Analysis of Nearly Incompressible Elasticity
abstract: Nearly incompressible materials arise in soft tissues, elastomers, gels, and other soft solids. Yet, numerical modeling remains challenging because displacement-based formulations can exhibit volumetric locking near incompressibility. Mixed displacement-pressure formulations address this difficulty but require compatible approximation spaces satisfying the inf-sup condition. In mixed formulations, discontinuous pressure spaces are attractive since pressure degrees of freedom can be condensed locally. In high-order isogeometric analysis, however, their Galerkin stability requires pressure-grid coarsening that increases with polynomial degree. Here, we develop a variational multiscale (VMS) stabilized mixed isogeometric formulation that retains this locality while substantially relaxing the restriction. The key observation is that VMS stabilization controls nonconstant elementwise pressure modes and is unconditionally stable with respect to its parameter, provided the elementwise constant pressure component satisfies the inf-sup condition. Consequently, for maximally continuous displacement splines, a pressure grid coarsened by a factor of two satisfies the constant-mode inf-sup criterion independently of polynomial degree. Local condensation then yields a displacement-only system, facilitating use in existing displacement solvers. The formulation is further extended to immersed isogeometric analysis with extended B-splines, pressure-cell aggregation, subdivision-based cut-cell quadrature, and weak enforcement of essential boundary conditions. Discrete inf-sup studies and convergence analyses in the Kirsch and Cook's membrane benchmarks demonstrate stability and show that the immersed treatment preserves mixed stability properties. The proposed framework therefore provides a local, high-order, and robust approach for nearly incompressible problems in mesh-conforming and immersed settings.

title: Quantitative Investigation of Spatial Inhomogeneity of Transition Metal Deposition in Commercial Automotive Cylindrical Cells under Overvoltage Conditions
abstract: Transition metal (TM) dissolution from the cathode and deposition on the anode in lithium−ion batteries is a key degradation mechanism, yet its spatial distribution in commercial cylindrical automotive-grade cells remains insufficiently understood. In this study on lithium−ion cells 18650 with a NMC811/graphite technology, we reveal a pronounced radial inhomogeneity in cathode metal deposition on the anode, with significantly higher accumulation in the inner windings of the jelly roll compared to the outer regions, identifying a critical vulnerability in the cell design while operating in…

title: General Synthesis of Inverse Opal Covalent Organic Framework Photonic Crystals
abstract: Constructing highly crystalline inverse opal covalent organic framework photonic crystals (IO COF PhCs) remains challenging due to the incompatibility between the spatial confinement required for inverse opal replication and the synthesis process of COFs. Inspired by the semi-solid chitin infiltration and confined solidification process in beetle photonic architectures, a solvent-free template-assisted melt pressing (STAMP) strategy is developed for the general synthesis of crystalline IO COF PhCs.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: AI-powered robotic laboratory paves the way for discovering next-generation heat-resistant coatings
abstract: Researchers have developed a self-driving laboratory that combines artificial intelligence and robotics to automate laboratory tasks, from accurately measuring and mixing chemical ingredients to high-temperature furnace processing and sample retrieval.

title: Tetrahydro-Dewar Pyridines (THDPs): Conformationally Programmable Piperidine Isosteres
abstract: Bioisosteric replacement is an indispensable tool in a medicinal chemist’s arsenal to strike a fine balance in multiparameter optimization campaigns and to deliver the best molecules for further preclinical development. The piperidine heterocycle is a valuable motif but often requires bioisosteric replacement to improve its ADME (absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion) profile. Despite recent advances in the field, practitioners still rely on the limited pool of commercially available piperidine isosteres that often have imperfect geometrical overlay. Herein, we explore tetrahydro-Dewar pyridines (THDPs) as rigid, programmable isosteres of piperidines. These building blocks are readily accessible from dihydro-Dewar pyridines (DHDPs), which can be synthesized from pyridine in only two steps using batch or flow photochemistry. Developed synthetic routes provide access to new building blocks and bifunctional linkers suitable for incorporation into various structural contexts. By applying the THDP scaffold to three distinct classes of kinase inhibitors, we demonstrate that THDPs offer a robust solution for testing advanced SAR hypotheses by stabilizing exit vectors while preserving physicochemical properties.

title: The Intersection of Allostery and Induced Proximity through the E3 Ligase Cereblon
abstract: Allostery modulates protein function through domains that are distinct from a protein’s orthosteric active site. In a therapeutic context, allosteric ligands provide mechanisms to overcome resistance, improve selectivity, and act cooperatively with orthosteric ligands. Separately, induced proximity modalities alter protein function by inducing an interaction between a target protein and an effector protein, like the E3 ligase substrate adapter cereblon (CRBN), which promotes the proteasomal degradation of the target. CRBN ligands that bind at the thalidomide-binding domain have seeded versatile chemical platforms for molecular glue degraders and proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs). CRBN gains its remarkable inducible substrate scope through conformational shifts that can be mediated by allosteric ligands to alter protein degradation outcomes. We merge the intersection of allostery with induced proximity modalities by examining it first in the context of allosteric pharmacology and second in the context of targeted protein degradation with CRBN, highlighting how lessons learned from allostery with other therapeutic targets could inform emerging opportunities for allosteric modulation of induced proximity events. This intersection of allostery and induced proximity at CRBN conceptually unites two major chemical means of changing protein fate, bringing the potential for highly selective and potent chemical modalities for a greater part of the proteome closer to reality.

title: EVA-Flow: Learning Shared Chemistry for Unified Environment-Aware Molecular Conformation Generation
abstract: Molecular 3D structures underpin simulations of thermodynamics, kinetics, crystallization, and nucleation, making their accurate prediction central to drug discovery and materials design. However, molecular geometry can change dramatically across environments. Existing models either ignore environmental effects or train separate models for each environment. We hypothesize that transfer learning across contexts is possible for conformer generation and that a general model will perform better when training data are limited, as in ligand binding and crystallization. We introduce EVA-Flow, a unified framework for environment-aware molecular conformation generation that learns shared chemical structure and adapts it through environment-conditioned generative modeling. Across vacuum, protein-ligand docking, solvation, and crystal packing, pretraining and cross-environment finetuning provide their largest gains in the three data-scarce settings. Evaluation against multiple reference conformations shows that EVA-Flow covers a broad range of solvation conformations. Analyses of molecules shared across environments support its ability to generate different conformations for the same molecule in different environments.

title: Subpercent accuracy in molecular electric quadrupole coupling: nuclear-size and relativistic effects in RaF
abstract: We report a benchmark study of the electric-quadrupole hyperfine interaction in the electronic ground state of the RaF molecule, including finite-nuclear-size effects. The calculations include relativistic effects using the Dirac-Coulomb-Breit Hamiltonian and electron correlation up to perturbative quadruple excitations within the coupled cluster framework. At the achieved level of accuracy, penetration of the electronic density into the finite nuclear quadrupole distribution produces a non-negligible correction to the usual electric field gradient (EFG) description at the center of the nucleus and must be considered. At a fixed rms charge radius, the EFG is much less sensitive to the shape of the monopole nuclear charge distribution: electron wavefunctions computed using the Gaussian and Fermi nuclear charge models yield nearly identical EFGs. The recommended effective EFG parameter for the $X\,{}^{2}Σ_{1/2}$ electronic ground state is $\langle q\rangle_0=-5.178(21)$ a.u., with an estimated uncertainty reduced by an order of magnitude compared to previous studies. Combined with future measurements of electric-quadrupole hyperfine coupling constants in RaF, this result can be used to determine the nuclear quadrupole moments of Ra isotopes with record precision.

title: Structure, Not Sequence: Tracking and Validating Folding Mechanisms in ESMFold's Trunk with Sparse Autoencoders
abstract: Structure predictors like ESMFold fold proteins using neural network computation and have transformed structural biology. However, the driving mechanism from amino-acid (AA) sequence to 3D structure is insufficiently understood, and biological meaning remains locked in the dense network. Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) have shown promising results in obtaining interpretable concept features over an overcomplete basis of intermediate protein sequence-model representations. Yet folding models, which predict physical shape from AA sequence semantics, have no such account. We hypothesize that the features carrying the folding computation evolve in the 3D structural regression process. In this paper, we interpret the folding trunk in three steps. First, a pilot analysis on the representation distribution across modules and recycles locates distinct spatial computation in the trunk. Second, the dictionaries expose a division of labor: the single representation carries inherited semantics, and the pair representation computes the pairwise geometry. Third, we interpret the dictionary at scale with a reasoning language model, trace how the concepts compose across blocks by gradient-based attribution, and follow the interpreted code to the model's folding output, verifying where the computation aligns with, or departs from, known biochemistry. Together, the sparse dictionaries we train capture the relational geometry the trunk computes beyond the sequence model, and their concept activations forecast the model's own fold quality, turning the black-box folding trunk into a sparse, interpretable, and scientifically verifiable circuit.

title: Spin Rectification in Series and Parallel Networks of Ferromagnets
abstract: We present the experimental study of spin rectification in parallel and series networks of ferromagnetic conductors. The networks were composed of Ni36Fe64 elements (wires) which, when subject to ferromagnetic resonance (FMR), develop a small spin-rectification photovoltage. We found that the effect of spin rectification can be modeled as an increase in resistance of the ferromagnetic elements and closely follows the usual dependence of total network resistance in series and parallel electric circuits: the total spin-rectification photovoltage in ferromagnetic wires connected in series is equal to the algebraic sum of contributions from individual wires, while in the parallel connection one needs to add the reciprocals of the individual contributions. Our results support a simple way to control and manipulate the magnitude of spin-rectification photovoltage in multi-element spintronic devices.

title: Exciton-driven coherent dressing in transient absorption
abstract: While coherent excitons have recently been observed to dress electronic states in time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (tr-ARPES), exciton-driven dressing in optical spectroscopy remains largely unexplored. This work develops a theoretical and computational approach to exciton-driven dressing effects in transient absorption spectroscopy in the time-dependent adiabatic GW formalism and derives two symmetry- and band topology-protected selections rules for exciton-dressed transient absorption, unique from tr-ARPES. We then numerically calculate exciton-dressed transient absorption spectra of monolayer MoS2 and demonstrate the selection rules and their lifting after symmetry breaking.

title: New molecular and historical evidence on ancient Egyptian embalming
abstract: Mumia vera aegyptiaca was a mummy-derived medicinal substance widely used in medieval and early modern medicine, yet its material composition and biological activity remain poorly understood. Here, we integrate Egyptological and pharmaceutical-historical analysis of 41 textual sources with LC-MS/MS-based metabolomics, molecular networking, machine-learning-assisted annotation, and bioactivity testing to investigate ancient Egyptian embalming materials and historical Mumia vera samples.
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: From Motion to Meaning: A Systematic Review of Motion Tracking in XR-based Experimental Psychology
abstract: Immersive technologies such as Virtual Reality (VR), Augmented Reality (AR), and Mixed Reality (MR) are being increasingly used in experimental psychology because they enable controlled environments while simultaneously producing high-frequency motiontracking data from headsets, controllers, and body trackers. These motion traces provide continuous behavioral signals that may reflect affective, behavioral, and cognitive processes during human-human, human-computer, and human-virtual human interactions.
venue: IEEE transactions on visualization and computer graphics

title: Confinement, registry and spin in chromium migration between graphene layers
abstract: We compare the migration of a single Cr atom on monolayer graphene, between AB-stacked layers and between AA-stacked layers, with one first-principles protocol (PBE+D3(BJ), one cell family, registry anchors and spin-state search). We find three main results. First, on the surface and in the AB gallery Cr stays magnetic and moves almost freely. On the surface the C-C bridge is the minimum in 4x4 and 5x5 cells, and the highest point we sample on a hop lies 10 meV above it (5x5). In the AB gallery Cr sits on the inversion centres of the bilayer, which form a kagome net, and hops between them over 15 meV with a moment of about 4.32 $μ_B$. Second, in the AA gallery the minimum is a nonmagnetic $η^6$-$η^6$ sandwich that pulls the layers together. Leaving it requires opening the gallery and switching Cr to a moment of 4-5 $μ_B$, so we map the path with separately relaxed spin branches. The barrier estimate is 636 meV in a 3x3 cell but 260 and 185 meV in 5x5 cells with the far-field spacing pinned and free, and it is not yet converged. At 300 K, with equal prefactors and if the spin change is not rate-limiting, Cr hops between AA layers 3-4 orders of magnitude more slowly than between AB layers, using the 5x5 AA estimates and the 3x3 AB band. These AA numbers are specific to PBE+D3: an on-site U of 1.0 eV on Cr d already makes the magnetic states the AA ground state. Third, Cr binds 246-666 meV more strongly in AA than in AB registry, so the fast AB hop requires that the layers keep their Bernal registry around Cr.

title: Learning the Chronology of Materials Discovery for Synthesizability Prediction
abstract: High-throughput computational and generative approaches are proposing candidate materials far faster than they can be synthesized, making it increasingly important to identify which hypothetical materials are likely to be experimentally realizable. Positive-unlabeled (PU) learning has emerged as a representative framework for synthesizability prediction, yet existing approaches treat experimentally reported materials as a static collection, overlooking the historical trajectory of materials discovery and the diverse practical factors that have driven its progress. Here we introduce ChronoSyn, a chronology-aware machine learning model that jointly learns synthesizability and the relative reporting order of known materials through a shared composition representation. Incorporating discovery chronology provides additional supervision beyond conventional synthesizability labels, improving prediction performance and enabling ChronoSyn to identify experimentally realizable compositions more effectively than baseline models. Applied to approximately 50 million hypothetical compositions, ChronoSyn identifies chemically coherent high-scoring families that include experimentally reported compositions unseen during training. These results highlight the chronology of materials discovery as an informative learning signal and suggest that the path along which known materials were discovered can point the way to those that will be discovered in the future.

title: Anisotropic Structural and Magnetic Response in Sm$_2$Ir$_8$Al$_{31}$: Al-Sublattice Reconstruction upon Sm Substitution
abstract: Chemical pressure plays a critical role in determining the crystal structures and physical properties of intermetallic compounds.
