Here, we report the synthesis, crystal structure, and physical properties of Sm$_2$Ir$_8$Al$_{31}$, a structural analog of UIr$_4$Al$_{15}$, in which the smaller 5f uranium atoms are replaced by larger 4f samarium atoms. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals a tetragonal $\sqrt{2}\times\sqrt{2}\times1$ superstructure with space group $P\bar{4}2_1m$, derived from a UIr$_4$Al$_{15}$-like average structure with space group $P4_2/nmc$. Comparison with UIr$_4$Al$_{15}$ shows that chemical pressure from U-to-Sm substitution produces a strongly anisotropic structural response rather than a uniform expansion of the Ir-Al framework. While one Ir coordination environment undergoes only modest changes, the other exhibits substantial local rearrangement. The Al sublattice primarily accommodates these structural distortions, with selected Al sites showing positional splitting, anisotropic atomic displacement ellipsoids, and partial occupancies, resulting in an Al-rich composition of approximately Sm$_2$Ir$_8$Al$_{31}$. Magnetic susceptibility measurements reveal a direction dependence, including a broad anomaly near 50 K for selected magnetic-field orientations. However, the absence of corresponding anomalies in heat capacity, electrical resistivity, and lattice parameters suggests that this feature is more consistent with an anisotropic magnetic crossover than a bulk thermodynamic phase transition. These results highlight how chemical substitution at the f-element site can induce Al-sublattice reconstruction and modify the magnetic response within a closely related Ir-Al structural framework.

title: RPAx Instabilities from Ground- and Excited-State References
abstract: Random-phase approximation with exchange (RPAx) calculations based on ground- or excited-state references can yield complex excitation energies, causing the corresponding RPAx correlation energy to become complex as well. In this work, we investigate the origin of these complex energies using \ce{H2} in the 6-31G basis set as a minimal model. For the ground-state restricted Hartree-Fock reference, complex roots emerge at the well-known triplet instability associated with the appearance of a lower-lying unrestricted, symmetry-broken solution. For excited-state references, we identify two distinct mechanisms leading to complex excitation energies. The first is similarly associated with symmetry breaking. The second arises when a positive-energy excitation becomes degenerate with the positive-energy de-excitation associated with a negative-energy transition. Finally, we demonstrate the practical implications of these findings for spin-flip Bethe-Salpeter equation calculations of cyclobutadiene and state-specific core-ionization calculations for selected systems. These examples show that, in the absence of the relevant instabilities, methods sharing the generalized eigenvalue structure of RPAx can be applied to excited-state references without resorting to the Tamm-Dancoff or core-valence separation approximations, while retaining real excitation energies.

title: A structural screen for candidate polyphosphate binding surfaces in human membrane associated proteins
abstract: Inorganic polyphosphate (polyP) can alter protein function through noncovalent binding, yet its partners among human membrane associated proteins remain poorly characterized. PolyP is recognized through two modes: a structure-based mode driven by charge complementarity with sites assembled by protein folding, and a more recently defined sequence-based mode at histidine and lysine rich tracts. The sequence determinant is well defined and directly searchable; the structure-based mode has few characterized examples and no systematic search method, because its residues leave no contiguous sequence signature. Broad experimental binding screens are especially demanding for integral membrane proteins, which require specialized conditions. We therefore developed a computational workflow that searches predicted structures for surfaces able to accommodate a phosphate chain. We designed custom scores that integrate surface electrostatics, docking results and structural confidence to prioritize candidates. From 19,481 completed docking searches on 5,648 AlphaFold models representing 2,925 UniProt protein entries, we nominated 82 entries as candidates for noncovalent polyP binding. Predicted polyP contacts in 18 candidate entries overlapped experimentally characterized functional residues, linking the predicted interfaces to established sites of ligand recognition, regulation and membrane attachment. The workflow ranks computational results rather than measuring binding, providing specific targets for experimental investigation.

title: Physical structure as an organizing principle for universal Hamiltonian learning
abstract: Density functional theory (DFT) gives the electronic structure of materials, but its cost limits large-supercell calculations and materials screening. Machine-learned Hamiltonians bypass the self-consistent cycle but are usually system-specific; universal ones could cover new compositions and disordered solids. Such models must generalize across chemistry and keep downstream properties physical, while staying inexpensive for large cells. Here we introduce UniTB, a universal E(3) equivariant Hamiltonian representation framework that integrates physical priors rooted in density-functional tight-binding theory with deep learning. UniTB's network, which corrects a prior Hamiltonian, generalizes across chemistry through a mixture of experts routed by that prior and a charge-equilibration head as in self-consistent-charge tight binding. A projection bounds band shifts from the prior, suppressing spurious states and keeping downstream properties physical. We provide the fastest SO(2) tensor-product GPU kernels for the network. The variant UniTB-Flash assembles its prior from two-center tables at $O(N)$ cost for $N$ atoms, against $O(N\log N)$ on a grid. Trained on 29,242 crystals, UniTB reaches a 0.48 meV matrix-element error on nonmagnetic test crystals spanning 68 elements. Without amorphous training data, both models agree with DFT optics and conductivity of amorphous Ge-Sb-Te. UniTB-Flash ranks candidates with no significant difference from UniTB, whose property values are more accurate; together they screen 16,195 crystals for five application domains of industrial relevance.

title: A Hybrid Brownian Dynamics-kinetic Monte Carlo Framework for Coupled Magnetic and Rotational Dynamics of Nanoparticles
abstract: Simulating the coupled magnetic and rotational dynamics of suspended magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) over experimentally relevant timescales remains computationally demanding, particularly under low-frequency alternating magnetic fields. Here, we develop a hybrid Brownian Dynamics--kinetic Monte Carlo (BD--kMC) framework that combines thermally activated magnetic switching with particle rotation while retaining local fluctuations of the magnetic moment. These fluctuations are incorporated through Metropolis Monte Carlo (MC) sampling, allowing the moment to depart from the energy minima and thereby capturing the thermally averaged anisotropy torque that governs particle rotation. To preserve the distinction between local fluctuations and magnetic reversals, a barrier-trapping criterion confines MC trial moves to the current energy well, leaving thermally activated switching to the kMC process. For non-interacting single-domain MNPs, comparison with stochastic Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert (LLG) simulations demonstrates agreement in the equilibrium torque and stationary easy-axis orientation, including the field-driven transition from predominantly perpendicular to parallel alignment. The resulting BD--kMC framework provides an efficient approach to coupled magnetic and Brownian Dynamics, reducing the computational cost of exploring the long timescales relevant to low-frequency magnetic applications.

title: A 3D-$Δ$PDF-like measure for hidden anisotropy in disordered materials
abstract: We introduce a simple correlation function for quantifying hidden local anisotropy in disordered materials. Developed in analogy with the three-dimensional difference pair distribution function (3D-$Δ$PDF), our approach identifies structural correlations that are lost through averaging over bulk symmetry. The same approach might be applied to models of disordered crystals, amorphous materials, and liquids alike.

title: Coulomb- and exchange-driven redistribution of spectral correlations
abstract: Electronic correlations reorganize not only the energies of individual electronic states but also the collective structure of the spectrum. Here, first-principles density functional theory calculations combined with random-matrix spectral statistics are used to examine this reorganization in gamma-Ce within a static spin-polarized DFT+U+SOC description. We distinguish the effects of the Coulomb interaction U from those of the exchange interaction J by analyzing nearest-neighbor spacings, reduced spacing ratios, band velocities, and band curvatures across the Ce-4f manifold. Increasing U does not produce a monotonic transition between Poisson- and Wigner-Dyson-like statistics; instead, the region of strongest level repulsion migrates across the 4f manifold as the interaction increases. Exchange produces a qualitatively different response. At fixed U, strongly repulsive and strongly clustered spectral regions coexist within the same 4f manifold even while the total spin moment and 4f occupation remain nearly unchanged. The clustering persists after resolving the spectrum into its dominant j = 5/2 and j = 7/2 components and differs strongly between calculations having the same numerical value of U-J. Within the present DFT+U+SOC description, the spectral response therefore depends on the separate Coulomb and exchange interactions and cannot be represented completely by a single effective U-J parameter. These results show that energy- and character-resolved spectral statistics expose correlation-driven electronic reorganization that is hidden by conventional integrated observables.

title: Environmental numerical models for predicting chemical transport and fate: From multimedia mass balance to machine learning
abstract: The increasing release of persistent and emerging chemicals into the environment has intensified the need for robust frameworks capable of predicting their transport, fate, and environmental behavior across multiple spatial and temporal scales. Over the past decades, environmental multimedia mass-balance models have played a key role in mechanistic simulations of chemical fate. Rapid advances in machine learning (ML) have introduced data-driven alternatives with enhanced capacity for handling high-dimensional, nonlinear datasets. The relative strengths, limitations, and appropriate application domains of these two paradigms remain insufficiently discussed. We examine classical and emerging numerical environmental models for chemical transport and fate, with a focus on multimedia mass-balance models and machine learning. We review the theoretical foundations, structures, and applications of widely used mass-balance models at local, regional, and global scales. We evaluate recent ML applications in parameter estimation, concentration prediction, source identification, and degradation modeling. We synthesize these models according to their thermodynamic basis, spatial segmentation, temporal treatment, and chemical applicability. We highlight the differences in model interpretability, data dependence, uncertainty propagation, and policy relevance. We identify key limitations that affect model reliability, including limited availability and uncertainty of parameters, incomplete characterization and propagation of uncertainty, and restricted generalization beyond the model assumptions or training data. We further discuss emerging hybrid strategies that integrate machine learning with mechanistic mass-balance models. When appropriately designed, independently validated, and accompanied by uncertainty analysis, these approaches can potentially improve parameterization, reduce systematic bias, and support scenario-based projections; however, they may also introduce additional uncertainty associated with ML predictions and model coupling. This review provides a methodological reference for future environmental fate modeling, supporting the development of more reliable tools for predicting the environmental fate of chemicals and for decision-making.

title: Intercalator effects on DNA loop extrusion by SMC proteins
abstract: Intercalating dyes are widely used to visualize DNA in single-molecule experiments, but their effects on DNA-processing proteins remain incompletely characterized. Here, we study the effects of intercalators on DNA loop extrusion by SMC complexes. Intercalating dyes become fluorescent upon DNA binding, enabling direct visualization of extruded DNA loops. As dye intercalation alters the biophysical properties of DNA by lengthening and unwinding it, we examine how that modifies loop extrusion. We systematically characterize the effects of intercalators, and find that they stiffen DNA, partly neutralize its charge, and can substantially reduce the binding and ATPase activity of SMCs. We assess four dyes and conclude that SYBR Gold and SYTOX Orange are less invasive intercalators than SYTOX Green or YOYO-1. While loop extrusion is qualitatively not affected by intercalation, quantitative values for SMC binding and looping rates differ significantly from those in the absence of intercalators. We present a new dye-free loop-extrusion assay (utilizing local fluorescent spots along DNA), and find that loop extrusion proceeds at 1.75{+/-}0.26 kb/s for S. cerevisiae condensin without dyes, while adding intercalators leads to a two-fold lower rate. Our findings establish that intercalators quantitatively modify loop extrusion parameters, and we offer practical recommendations for minimizing their impact.

title: Quantum Ghost Spectroscopy Reveals Hidden Coherence in Molecular Aggregates
abstract: Ultrafast spectroscopy of complex molecules has been achieved under light–matter coupling by the use of laser pulses and single photons. Yet, the excited-state dynamics essential to photochemistry is suffering from the convolution of multiple relaxation pathways and limited resolution in nonlinear signal, which still remain challenging. To address these, we develop time-resolved quantum ghost spectroscopy (tr-QGS) with entangled light, which enables a background-free detection of excited-state emission while offering precise control over temporal resolution. We apply this approach to perylene bisimide (PBI-1) trimers by combining a quantum description of light-molecule interaction with time-dependent density matrix renormalization group (TD-DMRG) simulations. This explicitly includes five vibrational modes and nonadiabatic coupling between electronic states. Our simulations reveal that tr-QGS captures electronic coherence oscillating at 0.6 eV for ∼50 fs, a signature of nonadiabatic coupling that was obscured in time-resolved measurements. Moreover, we observe a direct transfer from electronic to vibrational coherence at 200 fs, providing real-time visualization of vibronic relaxation pathways. Photon entanglement eliminates background noise and ground-state bleaching artifacts, which plague time-resolved measurements. These results establish tr-QGS as a transformative tool for interrogating nonadiabatic dynamics in molecular aggregates, light-harvesting complexes, and photocatalysts, offering a route to reveal quantum coherence effects in chemistry with unprecedented precision.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Evaluation of upper-scale mechanical parameters of particulate aluminum-based nanocomposites from molecular simulations
abstract: This paper focuses on the numerical and analytical determination of the mechanical parameters of aluminum-matrix nanocomposites using atomistic-scale simulations within a multiscale modeling framework. Molecular statics simulations were employed to evaluate the tensile and compressive behavior of Al based composites reinforced with nanosized alumina particles. Two classes of atomistic models were investigated. First, a unit-cell model containing a single Al2O3 monocrystal embedded in an aluminum matrix was used to examine the influence of the volume fraction of the ceramic inclusion on the effective mechanical properties. Second, a polycrystalline RVE model comprising an alumina particle was analyzed to assess the effect of the number of Al grains on effective properties. For each case, the mechanical response was characterized by stress-strain curves, enabling the identification of upper-scale material parameters associated with the elastic regime (bulk, shear and Young's modulus) and the damage stage (ultimate strength, ultimate strain, and failure strain). The isotropized elastic constants evaluated from molecular simulations were compared with classical Voigt-Reuss-Hill bounds to assess their applicability in the elastic regime. Finally, atomistic-scale simulation outputs provided insight into the dominant deformation/damage mechanisms (brittle versus ductile) and fracture modes (transgranular versus intergranular).

title: Symmetry-resolved fermionic correlations in iron-oxide ground spaces
abstract: Symmetries of quantum systems provide a natural way to organize the eigenspaces of many-body Hamiltonians. When degeneracies exist, however, they play a more subtle role as different sets of symmetry operators can resolve the same energy subspace into states with very different correlation properties. We study this interplay using a sequence of FeO and Fe$_2$O$_2$ models. For a Hubbard model of FeO, the ground space is 16-fold degenerate. Resolving it by local magnetizations gives a basis of Slater determinants, while total-spin quantum numbers select entangled and non-Gaussian states from the same ground manifold. Adding density-density Hund interactions breaks the independent spin rotations and reduces the ground space to a spin-reversal pair with maximal magnetization. These states are extremely close to Slater determinants in their natural occupations, yet have finite two-body cumulants and conserved-operator algebras whose orbit dimensions differ substantially from the Slater values. Fe$_2$O$_2$ provides a larger example in which spatial mode entanglement can be substantial while fermionic non-Gaussianity remains weak, with the conserved-operator structure again distinguishing the state from the corresponding Slater transformation class. Together, these examples show that symmetry resolution, mode entanglement, reduced-density-matrix correlations, and conserved-operator structure provide complementary information about interacting and degenerate electronic ground states.

title: Learning on-the-fly quasi-stationarity diagnostics from low-dimensional surrogates
abstract: Accelerated dynamics methods, such as parallel replica dynamics, require estimates of the decorrelation time, after which a process trapped in one of its metastable states is distributed according to the quasi-stationary distribution (QSD). In a method proposed by Binder, Lelièvre and Simpson, decorrelation times are defined by coupling a particle approximation of the non-linear conditioned probability flow of the process with MCMC-inspired diagnostics. We explore an alternative to MCMC diagnostics, based on coarse-graining of non-linear probability flows and simulation-based inference. We first develop a coarse-graining framework for killed Markov jump processes conditioned on survival, proving uniform-in-time, non-asymptotic estimates approximating the non-linear probability flow of the true process by the non-linear flow of a surrogate process, defined with a collective variable. The framework does not assume reversibility of the true process, and also gives bounds which scale explicitly in an adiabatic regime. Motivated by these results, we then construct a quasi-stationarity diagnostic using simulation-based inference: a recurrent neural network (RNN), trained on particle approximations of non-linear effective flows, estimates posterior probabilities of decorrelation. The learned diagnostic is then transferred to collective-variable traces of high-dimensional particle approximations. We investigate the behavior and robustness of this diagnostic on a set of numerical experiments, comparing it to the MCMC diagnostic of Binder et al.\ on both synthetic examples and a molecular system, in and out of its training prior distribution. When its prior assumptions hold, the RNN diagnostic outperforms the MCMC diagnostic in ROC analysis, is less conservative, fails less often, and has an interpretable decision threshold.

title: How Much Does the Hint Matter? Scope Conditions for Hindsight Self-Distillation in Financial Reasoning
abstract: Financial institutions operating under data-residency constraints are restricted to open-weight models small enough to locally host, which trail frontier systems on multi-step quantitative reasoning. On-policy distillation narrows such gaps by supervising a student on its own rollouts, but traditional OPD requires a strong external teacher, and on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) conditions on a full reference solution. We ask how much of that signal is necessary. We present Fin-SD, a localized hindsight self-distillation recipe for multi-step reasoning. Given a problem the student fails, the student itself identifies the first incorrect reasoning step and writes a short critique of that step. We truncate the student's trajectory immediately before the error (aiming to obtain a correct prefix), condition a frozen copy of the student on the same prefix plus the hint, and distill that hint-conditioned teacher into the student over a short rollout under reverse KL. No external model contributes a gradient. We apply Fin-SD to GPT-OSS-20B on a custom multi-step financial reasoning benchmark that requires deriving formula inputs from realistic scenarios via accounting conventions. We find: (i) replacing the critique with a generic-feedback control matches Fin-SD's entire 3.03 pp accuracy gain over the base model on the FinanceReasoning Hard subset, suggesting the gain comes from where supervision is applied, not hint content; (ii) the model writing the hint does not need to be stronger than the model receiving it: hints from same-family GPT-OSS-120B, at roughly 6x the parameters, yield no materially greater benefits than self-written hints; and (iii) Fin-SD matches on-policy self-distillation from full reference solutions on accuracy while generating 9.5% fewer tokens. With Fin-SD, general reasoning on MMLU-Pro and a fourteen-metric compliance audit on FinTrust show no material regression.

title: STEM-Bank-26: An Open Dataset of Analytical Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy Images and Spectra
abstract: Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) is a versatile, multi-modal method for studying materials at the nanoscale. It integrates multiple signal sources to provide atomic resolution imaging alongside spectroscopy for elemental composition and electronic structure. Despite its utility, few datasets spanning multiple years of data have been published. We introduce STEM-Bank-26, a 929 GB open dataset of 37,921 STEM images that spans 1,095 material samples across 1,499 sessions and includes energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) or electron-energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) data for 65.5% of sessions. We extract microscope control trajectories by comparing metadata between sequential images and provide tools for building similar datasets from archival data. To our knowledge, this is the largest openly available dataset that integrates experimental STEM, EDS and EELS data across a broad distribution of samples and sessions.

title: Harnessing Surface Wrinkling Instability for Visualizing Dynamic Chemistry in Polymer Networks
abstract: Studying dynamic chemical behaviors is fundamental to understanding and regulating the dynamic responses and functions of polymer materials. However, real-time, intuitive, and selective visualization of these molecular processes─particularly when multiple dynamic motifs coexist─remains a major challenge. Herein, we introduce surface wrinkles as a visualization platform that directly translates dynamic chemical behaviors in polymers into observable macroscopic morphological changes.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Comparing Nuclear Reaction Coordinates Driving Photoinduced Proton-Coupled Electron and Energy Transfer
abstract: Proton transfer is coupled to electron transfer or electronic excitation energy transfer in proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) and proton-coupled energy transfer (PCEnT) reactions, respectively. Although photoinduced PCET and PCEnT have been studied extensively in anthracene–phenol–pyridine molecular triads, the nuclear reaction coordinates for these two pathways are still unknown. Herein, we identify the nuclear reaction coordinates for PCET and PCEnT in the triads by sampling the seam space between the relevant intersecting diabatic states. The reaction coordinate has contributions mainly from anthracene and phenol for PCET but involves the entire triad, including pyridine, for PCEnT. Both reaction coordinates involve motions related to contraction of the phenol C–O bond as well as motions within the anthracene rings that differ for PCET and PCEnT due to different charge distributions. The proton acceptor motion contributes more to the PCEnT than the PCET reaction coordinate. Both PCET and PCEnT reactions are concerted in that there is no stable intermediate, but they are both most likely asynchronous. Our analysis also suggests that PCET proceeds through a conical intersection in its minimum energy pathway, whereas PCEnT moves through an avoided crossing. The quantum mechanical treatment of the transferring proton within a vibronically nonadiabatic framework suggests that the kinetic isotope effect may be greater for PCEnT than for PCET, although more extensive calculations are required for confirmation. Understanding the fundamental similarities and differences between PCET and PCEnT mechanisms will help guide the design of proton-coupled systems that favor either charge transfer or energy transfer.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Mechanism-Driven Size Optimization of Fully Exposed Rh Cluster Catalysts for Butane Dehydrogenation
abstract: Nonoxidative butane dehydrogenation offers a direct route to C4 olefins, yet it remains challenged by the need to promote C–H activation while ensuring olefin desorption and suppressing C–C cracking. Here, we report a mechanism-guided study that combines density functional theory calculations with experimental validation to rationally design Rh-based catalysts for butane dehydrogenation.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Multi-omics Breast Cancer Subtype Prediction and Discovery: A Systematic Review
abstract: Artificial intelligence models integrate molecular omics to reproduce breast cancer subtype labels or discover patient groups, but heterogeneous endpoints, cohorts, and validation hinder interpretation. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Europe PMC, and OpenAlex through 2026 September 8, supplemented by citation searching and targeted retrieval through Google Scholar and IEEE Xplore. Eligible studies combined at least 2 molecular omics in one machine-learning model for breast cancer subtype prediction or discovery. Findings were synthesized by endpoint without meta-analysis. Of 705 exported records, 301 duplicates were removed, 404 unique records were screened, and 70 studies were included. Fifty-seven addressed intrinsic subtype or Prediction Analysis of Microarray 50 (PAM50) prediction, and 11, subtype discovery or recovery. Sixty-two publications used The Cancer Genome Atlas Breast Invasive Carcinoma, and 9 used the Molecular Taxonomy of Breast Cancer International Consortium, demonstrating extensive reuse of limited patient populations. Among 59 supervised prediction studies, only 1 independently evaluated a complete multi-omics model in another cohort, and none reported prospective or nested full-pipeline validation. Calibration, uncertainty reporting, and external validation were uncommon, although 34 studies provided code or software. Among 11 discovery studies, 4 assessed resampling stability and 3 attempted independent subtype recovery. All 57 PAM50 studies used expression, and none reported excluding PAM50 classifier genes or close proxies. Thirty-nine included a matched expression-only baseline, but only one tested the complete model independently. Risk of bias was high in 48/59 prediction studies. Graph, hypergraph, attention, and uncertainty-aware models are increasingly used, but evidence of transportability and calibrated clinical value remains limited.

title: Background-Robust Static Hand Gesture Recognition with Synthetic Scene Compositing: A Grouped Fivefold Ablation Across Five CNN Backbones
abstract: Static hand gesture recognition models typically achieve high performance on small RGB datasets but exhibit reduced robustness as background complexity increases. This study investigates whether synthetic scene compositing can mitigate this vulnerability by employing a leakage-aware evaluation protocol. The proposed pipeline integrates alpha-matting-based foreground extraction with random scene compositing and is evaluated using a fivefold protocol that groups images at the image level, ensuring that augmented siblings from the same source image remain within the same fold.

title: Characterization and evaluation of the anti-streptococcal activity of a novel zoocin A-like endopeptidase for potential veterinary applications
abstract: The increasing prevalence of antimicrobial resistance among streptococci necessitates the development of alternative antibacterial strategies against veterinary pathogens. Here, we report the first comprehensive characterization of pre-ZooA_agal, a zoocin A-like bacteriolytic enzyme derived from Streptococcus agalactiae strain QMA0326. Both the proenzyme containing signal peptide (SP) pre-ZooA_agal and its mature variant containing the catalytic and target recognition domains (ZooA_agal) were successfully expressed and purified following the optimization of expression conditions.

title: Glycosylated steroidal saponins suppress HNSCC progression by targeting the RAS-ERK pathway
abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is characterized by high incidence, pronounced invasiveness and metastasis, and poor prognosis, underscoring an urgent need for novel and effective therapeutic strategies. Natural steroidal saponins serve as promising anti-tumor leads, yet prior work only reports their downstream ERK suppression, lacking upstream regulators and systematic glycosylation-related structure-activity relationship (SAR) analysis. This study focused on diosgenin and its two glycosylated derivatives.

title: Third harmonic generation in the transition metal trichalcogenides
abstract: The transition metal trichalcogenides (TMTs) are an interesting class of layered 2D materials that have strong anisotropic electrical and optical properties. We report on the polarization-dependent nonlinear optical response of exfoliated crystals at the third harmonic using non-resonant excitation with a 1560 nm femtosecond laser. All members of the TMT crystal family explored (ZrS3, HfS3, TiS3, and NbS3) display large anisotropy in their polarized third harmonic generation signal, with anisotropy ratios as large as chi_11/chi_22 ~ 6.5. From the expected nonlinear dependence of these monoclinic and triclinic crystals we extract the relative nonlinear susceptibility coefficients. We find that the anisotropy ratio is largest for ZrS3 and decreases across the family, a trend we associate with the proximity of the third harmonic energy to the strongly b-polarized absorption edge of each material. NbS3, the only triclinic crystal, displays a pronounced anisotropy in thick flakes that is strongly reduced in the thinnest flakes, which we attribute to a partial relaxation of the Peierls-type Nb-Nb dimerization that underlies the triclinic distortion. The large anisotropic nonlinear response in this crystal family sets it apart from other 2D materials and makes it particularly attractive for further investigation.

title: Beyond trial and error: Integrating computation, processing, and AI to design high-entropy alloys
abstract: Designing structural high-entropy alloys (SHEAs) means solving a problem with an enormous number of moving parts: which combinations of composition and processing conditions will yield the phases, microstructures, and mechanical properties a given application demands? Because these alloys mix multiple principal elements in comparable proportions, that question spans length and time scales that no single experiment or model can cover on its own.

title: Review of the design and development of MXene-based electrocatalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction
abstract: The oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is a critical half-reaction in fuel cells, but its slow kinetics demand the use of efficient and durable electrocatalysts. MXenes, a novel class of two-dimensional materials, have emerged as highly promising catalyst supports for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) due to their high electrical conductivity, abundant anchoring sites, adjustable surface properties, and excellent durability. This review offers an overview of recent advancements in the design and development of MXene-based electrocatalysts for the ORR.

title: Combining Single-Cell Data with Machine Learning Uncovers the Molecular Landscape of Keratoconus
abstract: PurposeKeratoconus (KC) is a progressive disorder characterized by corneal ectasia, corneal thinning, and conical protrusion, which can lead to diminished vision and corneal scarring. However, the molecular mechanism underlying KC has not yet been fully elucidated. In this study, we combined bioinformatics tools and experimental assays to uncover cell-type-specific pathogenic regulators and promising diagnostic biomarkers of KC.MethodsWe analyzed the KC-associated bulk mRNA expression dataset GSE151631 (19 KC, 7 controls) and the single-cell RNA sequencing dataset GSE285060 (5 KC, 3 controls)…

title: Expert lithological labels do not improve learning when used to predict marine sediment properties
abstract: Scientific drilling has produced large archives of physical, chemical and magnetic measurements linked to descriptions of the rock recovered. These archives are mostly incomplete: instruments sample at different intervals, recovery is partial, and destructive analyses preclude later measurement of the same material. We train an self-supervised embedding model on the LILY ocean drilling database using six routinely logged properties (bulk density, magnetic susceptibility, natural gamma radiation, and red, green and blue reflectance) across 236,963 observations from 296 boreholes, with a masked variational autoencoder that has a heteroscedastic Gaussian decoder and learnable mask tokens. The embeddings separate geologist-assigned lithologies as well as a variant trained with those labels, and increasing the weight on the labels degrades reconstruction while leaving classification unchanged. The labels are recoverable from the measurements geologists use to assign them, so training on them adds nothing. Lithological categories compress continuous measurements into classes, and compressing them discards what the measurements record about the processes that produced the rock. The embeddings also predict physical properties that were absent from training, on boreholes the model has never seen. While depth should account for this since sediments compact with burial, it does not. On held-out boreholes depth alone reaches a median $R^2$ of -0.02, against 0.20 for the embedding.

title: A thioester-thiol exchange reaction in Salmonella Invasion acyl carrier protein transfers the 4PP-bound acyl chain to a distal cysteine
abstract: Salmonella Typhimurium encodes two functionally distinct acyl carrier proteins: AcpP, involved in fatty acid synthesis, and the invasion acyl carrier protein (IacP), which mediates the acylation of SipB (Salmonella invasion protein B), a modification essential for SipB maturation and efficient host invasion. Despite growing insights, the IacP-dependent machinery governing acyl chain transfer remains largely enigmatic. Therefore, a multidisciplinary approach combining biochemistry and NMR was employed.

title: Nickel-Catalyzed Electroreductive Cross-Electrophile Coupling of Aryl/Alkenyl Triflates with Alkyl Bromides Assisted by an Organo-Mediator
abstract: Given the thermodynamic stability of the C(sp2)–O bond, the development of simple and efficient strategies for its functionalization holds significant practical value. In this study, we report an electroreductive, one-pot nickel-catalyzed cross-electrophile coupling (XEC) of aryl/alkenyl triflates with diverse (1°, 2°, and 3°) alkyl bromides. Rapid in situ generation of Ni0 species enables efficient activation of the C(sp2)–O bond, yielding a broad range of C(sp2)–C(sp3) coupling products.

title: Favorable Carrier Dynamics in a Narrow-Gap Layered Oxynitride Enable Efficient Molecular Hybrid CO2 Photoreduction
abstract: Efficient interfacial electron transfer from light-harvesting semiconductors to molecular catalysts remains a major challenge in molecular–semiconductor hybrid photocatalytic CO2 reduction, particularly for narrow-bandgap semiconductors, whose reduced thermodynamic driving force often requires assistance from metallic electron-transfer mediators such as Ag. Here, we show that, despite its narrow bandgap of 2.1 eV, the layered perovskite oxynitride K2LaTa2O6N (KLTON) functions as an effective semiconductor support for a supramolecular RuRu′ CO2-reduction catalyst without relying on Ag nanoparticles. The RuRu′/KLTON hybrid selectively converted CO2 to formate under visible-light irradiation with >99% selectivity, a turnover number of 691, and an apparent quantum yield of 6.1 ± 0.6% at 420 nm. Loading a small amount of Ag further increased the turnover number to 1077, but this 1.5-fold enhancement was modest compared with the larger Ag-induced activity enhancements reported for several conventional oxynitride-based hybrids, highlighting the weak Ag dependence of the KLTON-based system. Spatial photodeposition of Ag and MnOx revealed spatially differentiated surface redox reactivity on the terraced layered structure of KLTON, while time-resolved microwave conductivity and transient infrared absorption measurements showed favorable photogenerated-carrier dynamics and demonstrated that Ag loading modifies the electron dynamics of KLTON. Time-resolved emission measurements further revealed an additional nonradiative decay pathway at the Ru(II) photosensitizer/KLTON interface, consistent with interfacial electronic interaction without uniquely assigning its microscopic origin. These results identify favorable carrier dynamics and weak Ag dependence as key features of the KLTON-based molecular hybrid and highlight layered narrow-bandgap mixed-anion semiconductors as promising support materials for visible-light-driven molecular photocatalysis.

title: Competition Between Task Accuracy and Habitual Locomotor Behavior Underlies the Speed-Accuracy Trade-Off in Walking
abstract: The speed-accuracy trade-off is a hallmark feature of motor behavior, yet its underlying causes in cyclic, whole-body movements such as walking remain to be understood. In discrete, point-to-point movements, reduced accuracy at higher speeds is typically attributed to signal-dependent motor noise and an inability to use online error correction. Walking, however, may be governed by additional objectives, such as minimizing metabolic energy expenditure. To distinguish between these mechanisms, we tested young adults in a precision-walking task requiring them to match target step lengths across a range of treadmill speeds. Accuracy declined systematically as walking speed increased, demonstrating a locomotor speed-accuracy trade-off. Contrary to prevailing theory, removing online visual feedback of foot position did not affect this decline, indicating little contribution from visually guided error correction. Moreover, step-length variability, a task-specific measure of signal-dependent motor noise, decreased rather than increased with speed. Instead, faster walking produced progressively larger biases toward participants' habitual step lengths measured in the absence of targets. Because habitual step lengths are known to closely approximate energetically optimal values, these findings suggest energetic optimization, rather than motor noise or limitations associated with the use of online feedback, as the primary driver of the speed-accuracy trade-off during walking.

title: Polymorphic Structures of an Artificial Nucleocapsid Evolved from a Circularly Permuted Bacterial Protein Cage
abstract: Molecular self-assembly provides a route to nanoscale structures with defined sizes and shapes. Protein cages assembled from repeated subunits form compartments that can package molecular cargoes. Although amino acid substitutions can alter intersubunit interactions and cage architecture, how protein backbone connectivity relates to the cage architectures accessible during laboratory evolution remains unclear. Here we evolved an artificial nucleocapsid from a circularly permuted variant of Aquifex aeolicus lumazine synthase (AaLS). Laboratory evolution increased the yield of purified nucleocapsids relative to the progenitor, and the evolved variant, NC119-3, packaged its encoding mRNA. Cryo-electron microscopy revealed a heterogeneous population of cages, within which we resolved 180- and 210-subunit cage families composed of 36 and 42 pentamers, respectively. Within each resolved family, particles with the same subunit stoichiometry differed in the arrangement and orientation of their pentameric building blocks. A 2.90 [A] reconstruction of a tetrahedral 180-subunit cage further revealed that sequence-identical subunits adopt distinct conformations depending on their positions within the assembly. These pentamer-based architectures differ from the domain-swapped T = 4 cage previously reported for nucleocapsids evolved from an AaLS variant with a different circular permutation site. Together with previous work, these findings show that RNA-packaging nucleocapsids evolved from scaffolds with different backbone connectivity can adopt distinct cage architectures.

title: Machine learning dataset and benchmark for accurate T cell receptor–pHLA binding prediction
abstract: Hi-TPH is a large-scale hierarchical dataset that enables more accurate prediction of T cell receptor binding to antigens using protein language models and reveals how molecular components jointly contribute to prediction.

title: Keeping water molecules connected reduces carbon electrode corrosion
abstract: Carbon is inexpensive, conductive, and widely used in technologies such as fuel cells and water electrolyzers. But under strongly oxidizing conditions, carbon electrodes gradually corrode.

title: Decision-Dependent Adversarial Planning for Cyber-Resilient Solar-Rich Power Grids
abstract: The rapid expansion of solar photovoltaic (PV) capacity has exposed the grid to escalating cyber threats that exploit the growing digital footprint of renewable infrastructure. Existing joint planning methods for PV and battery energy storage systems (BESSs) largely optimize techno-economic performance without capturing how deployment decisions reshape cyber threats. Temporal aggregation can obscure seasonal operations and storage-state evolution, while plan-dependent attacks create a costly mixed-integer search.

title: Regulated Density of Atomic Cu Sites Dictates Switching from C1 to C2+ Products in CO Electroreduction
abstract: Single-atom catalysts (SACs) are generally considered C1-selective in CO2/CO electroreduction, as spatially isolated sites cannot efficiently sustain adjacent CO-derived intermediates required for C─C coupling. Here we show that this selectivity bias is not intrinsic to atomically dispersed Cu, but depends on single-atom site density. Across a series of Cu–N3O catalysts with different Cu site densities, increasing site density drives a clear selectivity crossover from H2 and CH4 formation to C2+ products.

title: Mechanistic Interpretability of LLM Behavior: A Survey
abstract: Mechanistic interpretability seeks to explain how internal computations produce large language model behaviors, yet findings remain fragmented across methods and behavioral domains. We survey 229 papers across five behavior families: epistemic, linguistic, reasoning, safety, and social behaviors. We introduce a framework distinguishing five levels of mechanistic evidence, from decodability to generalization. Our cross-behavior synthesis reveals recurring mechanisms, distinctions between representation and causal control, and limitations of existing explanations.

title: Glowing ghoul or chemical tool? The toxic chemistry behind Victorian séances
abstract: In November 1857, during a séance in Jersey City, the medium Leah Brown claimed her body produced luminous particles. So intense was the luminosity emanating from her, she recalled in her memoir, that it almost burned her hands. She rinsed her hands under a tap and then pushed them into the damp earth outside.

title: Ahead of their time: Restricted to pre-2018 research, AI flags hydrogen catalyst reported in later experiments
abstract: Researchers have used artificial intelligence to identify promising catalysts using only the scientific knowledge that was available years before their actual discovery. Their findings could accelerate the search for more efficient hydrogen production and other valuable chemical processes.
